# Encrypted PDF fixtures

These two-page documents contain only synthetic text and colored page edges.
They were created locally on 2026-11-03 with Python, pypdf 6.10.0 and
cryptography 50.0.0, using `generate.py`; no bank document or personal data was
used. PDF encryption is produced by pypdf, not by a custom test cipher.

| File | Encryption | User password |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `aes128.pdf` | Standard security handler, AES-128 | `fixture-pass-128` |
| `aes256.pdf` | Standard security handler, AES-256 | ` fixture-pass-256 ` (one leading and one trailing space) |

Both use the synthetic owner password `fixture-owner-only`. All these passwords
are public test data. The second password intentionally verifies that meaningful
spaces are preserved. The browser test uses the application's actual PDF.js
renderer and worker to open the committed encrypted bytes.

To regenerate, install the listed Python packages in a development virtual
environment and run `python3 tests/fixtures/pdf-password/generate.py`. Encryption
uses randomized salts/IVs, so regenerated bytes need not match previous hashes.
The ordinary build and CI require no PDF-generating Python dependencies.
